2027-data-engineering-predictions.note: Prediction round-ups aggregate many individual signals, and a few of these items were already circulating before the original 2026 posts. Treat the specific timelines as directional rather than commitments — the *durable* takeaway is the batch/stream convergence and AI-augmented pipeline operations, which every major warehouse vendor is shipping toward.
2027-data-engineering-predictions.author: Editorial team

data-mesh-implementation.note: Data mesh is the rare architectural idea whose *governance* layer (domain ownership, federated compute) outlives its technology hype. If you are adopting it in a regulated environment, map the domain boundaries against your RACI chart first: data contracts work only when the owning domain also owns the SLO.
data-mesh-implementation.author: Editorial team

feature-store-feast-vs-tecton.note: The vendor landscape here moves quickly — both projects have shifted their online/offline serving defaults since these comparisons were written. For a small team, a managed feature store often pays for itself in training-serving skew elimination alone; for a mature platform team, Feast on your own stack keeps the data plane under your control.
feature-store-feast-vs-tecton.author: Editorial team

data-observability-lineage.note: Lineage systems over-promise: most capture *syntactic* lineage (column-to-column) while the questions compliance teams ask are *semantic* (which business fact feeds this report). Budget for a manual semantic layer on top of automated discovery, or the DataOps investment will not satisfy an audit.
data-observability-lineage.author: Editorial team
